title: SOC2/ISO Posture Review - Millbrook Health
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 summary link
Share Trust Center access (controls mapping + org-level reports)
Samir to prepare POC plan for dedicated vs private deployment (latency/cost benchmarks)
Schedule follow-up in two weeks to review POC scope and security checklist
action_items: Ari Martinez - Share SOC2 Type II report, ISO summary, and Trust Center invite (due 2026-03-10)
Samir Patel - Draft POC test plan for dedicated/private deployments with expected latency/cost targets (due 2026-03-13)
Dana Lee - Send list of in-scope data types and residency constraints (due 2026-03-12)
Priya Singh - Confirm compliance stakeholders for controls mapping workshop (due 2026-03-11)
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 and ISO 27001 posture for Millbrook Health. Discussed trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit log retention, KMS/BYOK options, and private deployment requirements. Agreed next steps: share reports and Trust Center, Samir to prepare POC plan, customer to provide in-scope data residency constraints.
transcript:
00:00 Ari Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the SOC-two slash ISO posture review for Millbrook, um, hope that time still works, I see Dana and Marcus on the line.
00:18 Dana Lee: Yep, works for me, thanks Ari. Priya here as well, hey.
00:24 Marcus Reed: Hi all.
00:27 Samir Patel: Hey team, Samir from Redwood, I'm the SE on the thread, I'll focus on architecture and controls mapping.
00:35 Ari Martinez: Quick agenda, we'll run through our compliance artifacts, Trust Center access, highlight controls mapping between SOC 2/ISO, then dig into SSO/RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, and finally private/dedicated deployment considerations. Save time for Q&A.
00:55 Priya Singh: Awesome. We mostly want to validate controls coverage and what reports you can share, plus retention windows for logs and where data can live.
01:07 Ari Martinez: Totally. I'll share screen in a sec - but to start, as a quick note, Redwood has both SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 certificate; we maintain an external audit cycle and can provide the Type II report under NDA.
01:21 Dana Lee: Good. Is that the full Type II or a SOC 2 readiness pack?
01:27 Ari Martinez: It's the full Type II. We'll provide the redacted report plus an ISO 27001 summary. In the Trust Center we surface the controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our SOC controls to ISO controls and to the more technical configs - that's what most security teams use.
01:42 Omar Khalid: When you say Trust Center, is that a portal we can log into or a manual share?
01:47 Ari Martinez: It's a portal. We'll add Millbrook org-level access - you'll be able to download the reports, view our SOC controls mapping, change logs for cert renewals. We'll send an invite.
01:58 Marcus Reed: Are there any gaps we should be aware of? For example HIPAA related items, or anything that impacts PHI handling?
02:05 Samir Patel: Good question. Redwood's core platform is not a HIPAA-hosted product by default. For PHI workloads we typically recommend Private (VPC) deployment or a dedicated instance with specific BAAs and configuration. We'll note that in the controls mapping - but the SOC 2/ISO controls themselves cover a lot of the security baselines.
02:22 Dana Lee: Okay, we will follow up on HIPAA/BAA specifics.
02:27 Priya Singh: On logs - what is the retention period for audit logs, and can we configure longer retention?
02:34 Samir Patel: By default, audit logs in hosted are retained for 90 days in the console and longer in archived storage - we can provide exports for a year plus on request. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and can ship logs to your Splunk/Datadog or to a customer S3 for longer-term archival.
02:50 Dana Lee: And are logs tamper-evident?
02:54 Samir Patel: We provide append-only log streams with integrity checks; we can also ship signed log bundles for archives. There are some transcription notes, um, the term we use is append-only and we keep cryptographic hashes for integrity.
03:10 Marcus Reed: Great. Regarding SSO, do you support SAML or OIDC?
03:14 Ari Martinez: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. We integrate with Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace. RBAC is role-based with custom roles available on Dedicated/Private.
03:27 Dana Lee: Any limitations on SCIM provisioning fields?
03:31 Samir Patel: Mostly standard attributes; we can map custom attributes in Dedicated/private if needed.
03:36 Priya Singh: For RBAC, can we restrict access to specific model routes or datasets?
03:41 Lena Cho: Yes, we support per-route and per-model permissions on Dedicated and Private; hosted can do team-level RBAC and API token scoping. There are some small naming inconsistencies in older docs - we call them routes, sometimes 'endpoints' - sorry for that.
03:57 Omar Khalid: Encryption - how are keys managed? KMS? BYOK? HSM?
04:02 Samir Patel: Encryption at rest uses provider KMS by default (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault depending on region). For Private you can bring your own keys (BYOK) and integrate with your HSM/KMS. We also offer HSM-backed key wraps for Dedicated customers on request.
04:19 Dana Lee: Is there support for customer-managed keys in hosted?
04:22 Ari Martinez: For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS for enterprise customers - you can bring a key via KMS. For stricter needs we usually recommend Private.
04:33 Marcus Reed: Data residency: can we restrict where data is stored and processed?
04:38 Samir Patel: Yes - we support region pinning. Hosted offers region selection across our cloud regions, Dedicated gives a single-region control plane for your capacity, and Private gives you full control (on-prem or VPC). We'll need to capture which AWS regions you require.
04:52 Priya Singh: We need EU for EU patient data and US-East for US patients, and separate logging.
04:58 Samir Patel: Noted - we'll flag that for the POC.
05:02 Dana Lee: Controls mapping - will you share a matrix showing which SOC control maps to our ISO and to the feature/config we need to operate?
05:10 Ari Martinez: Yes, the Trust Center controls mapping is exactly that; it has columns for SOC 2 control, ISO 27001 clause, implementation references (e.g., RBAC config, audit log retention, key management links), and evidence artifacts. We'll add a mapping row for private/dedicated features where implementation differs.
05:28 Marcus Reed: Evidence artifacts - do you provide SRE runbooks or config snapshots?
05:33 Samir Patel: We provide architecture diagrams, runbook excerpts, and test evidence samples. For live customers we can provide queryable logs or signed exports under NDA.
05:42 Omar Khalid: For PII/PHI handling, how do you redact or avoid storage?
05:47 Samir Patel: On request we can enable prefix/KV caching rules and delta logging to avoid storing raw text in long-term stores; but specifics depend on the integration. For highest assurance we recommend Private with local data processing and no egress.
06:05 Dana Lee: Can you walk through an example controls mapping?
06:09 Ari Martinez: Sure. So SOC CC6 for access controls maps to ISO A.9 and then implementation is our SSO + RBAC model plus SCIM provisioning. Evidence is SSO config exports and user provisioning logs. For encryption controls, SOC common criteria map to ISO crypto controls and we point to KMS configuration and key rotation logs.
06:28 Priya Singh: About key rotation cadence, what's your default?
06:31 Samir Patel: We default to rotate platform keys yearly and customer-managed keys follow your KMS policies - you control rotation there. We also keep rotation audit history.
06:40 Marcus Reed: Auditing of admin actions - can we get a stream of admin events?
06:45 Lena Cho: Yes, admin events are included in the audit log stream. You can filter by actor and action and export to your SIEM in near real-time.
06:54 Dana Lee: Is MFA enforced for Redwood console access?
06:57 Ari Martinez: For Redwood employees yes, and for customer orgs we enforce MFA if using SSO; you can require MFA for all user logins via your IdP.
07:08 Priya Singh: About physical security for on-prem package - do you provide guidance?
07:12 Samir Patel: Our on-prem package comes with a deployment guide that enumerates physical security requirements; we obviously defer to your data center controls for the final implementation.
07:23 Dana Lee: How often do you run penetration tests and vulnerability scans?
07:27 Ari Martinez: External pen tests annually and internal vuln scans weekly with a triage process. We can share summaries and remediation timelines in the Trust Center.
07:36 Marcus Reed: For SLA and uptime, any security-related incident reporting?
07:40 Ari Martinez: Yes, we have incident response SLAs. We will notify customers per severity and provide postmortems in our incident channel and, for Dedicated/Private, add the required stakeholders into our incident bridge.
07:53 Omar Khalid: Regarding model data, will model fine-tuning happen on our data in hosted?
07:57 Samir Patel: By default, hosted does not fine-tune on customer data; we can enable fine-tuning in Dedicated/Private under customer-controlled buckets with explicit policies. We'll detail that in the POC doc.
08:10 Priya Singh: Any limitations with RBAC on hosted - can we create custom roles for compliance auditors?
08:16 Lena Cho: Hosted supports auditor roles with restricted read-only access to logs and reports; custom roles with very granular controls are better supported on Dedicated/Private.
08:25 Dana Lee: About backups - where are backups stored and how long?
08:29 Samir Patel: Backups are stored in encrypted object storage in the same region by default; retention varies by service but we can set retention policies per-customer for Dedicated/Private.
08:40 Marcus Reed: Do you have an allow-list for network egress or IP allow-lists?
08:44 Ari Martinez: We support IP allow-lists for API traffic and private links for Dedicated; Private gives you full network control inside your VPC.
08:53 Priya Singh: Any red flags or common gotchas customers see in the controls mapping?
08:58 Samir Patel: Often it's around assumptions - for example, hosted customers sometimes assume BYOK is available in all tiers; it's an enterprise feature. Also region pinning needs early configuration. We'll call those out.
09:12 Dana Lee: Great. Can you talk about cert rotation and evidence? We need audit history for last two years.
09:18 Ari Martinez: We can provide certificate rotation logs and key change history in the Trust Center as part of the evidence set; if you need two-year history we'll confirm archive availability but generally we keep rotation history for multi-year periods.
09:30 Omar Khalid: In terms of encryption algorithms, do you publish exact ciphers TLS and at-rest algorithms?
09:35 Samir Patel: Yes, TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers - we'll include the crypto spec in the Trust Center docs. At-rest uses AES-256 for object storage and envelope encryption.
09:46 Priya Singh: About employee access reviews - how frequent?
09:49 Ari Martinez: Quarterly access reviews, and we have automated access deprovisioning tied to SCIM and HR integrations.
09:56 Marcus Reed: Can you support periodic attestation exports for our auditors?
09:59 Samir Patel: Yes, we can provide attestation artifacts and signed evidence for auditors under NDA.
10:07 Dana Lee: Ok thanks. On the Trust Center access, what's the process for invite and permissions?
10:12 Ari Martinez: We'll send an org-level invite; admins from Millbrook will be able to add users. We'll provision a read-only compliance view and a deeper view for engineers.
10:21 Priya Singh: Would you also share a controls mapping workshop invite?
10:24 Ari Martinez: Yes we'll set up a 60-minute workshop to walk the controls mapping with your compliance and engineering teams.
10:31 Marcus Reed: For the POC, can you outline which tests you'll run for latency and data residency?
10:35 Samir Patel: We'll run throughput and p95/p99 latency tests under typical prompt distributions, test KV cache hit rates and prefix caching, and validate region pinning with sample data flows. We'll also measure token costs per 1k requests.
10:52 Dana Lee: Any benchmarking artifacts you can share from other customers?
10:55 Samir Patel: We have anonymized benchmark sheets and an internal runbook. We'll share anonymized results and an expected baseline for similar workloads.
11:07 Priya Singh: Are there any legal documents we need to sign before you share the full Type II report?
11:11 Ari Martinez: We usually require an NDA or an MSA addendum; we'll share the redacted PDF under NDA and then grant Trust Center access once NDAs are in place.
11:22 Marcus Reed: On the topic of vulnerabilities, what's your patch cadence for the runtime?
11:26 Samir Patel: Runtime security patches go out on a rolling schedule, critical patches are prioritized and we have hotfix procedures. For Dedicated/Private we coordinate maintenance windows.
11:36 Dana Lee: For Private on-prem installs, do you provide support for upgrades?
11:40 Ari Martinez: Yes, upgrade playbooks and remote assistance are part of our Private package. We also offer a managed upgrade option.
11:49 Priya Singh: A couple of quick clarifying Qs: can you set stricter log retention per dataset and separate logs per region?
11:55 Samir Patel: Yes, per-dataset routing and regional segregation of logs is achievable in Dedicated/Private; hosted has some constraints but we can route logs to customer-controlled endpoints per region.
12:09 Dana Lee: Great. Anything else on certification timelines?
12:12 Ari Martinez: Our next ISO surveillance audit is later this year - we'll surface the schedule in the Trust Center.
12:18 Marcus Reed: Ok, sounds good. Let's recap.
12:22 Ari Martinez: Recap: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO materials under NDA, invite you to Trust Center, Samir will draft POC plan focusing on dedicated vs private for latency/cost, Millbrook to provide data residency and in-scope items, schedule controls mapping workshop.
12:40 Dana Lee: That works. Priya, Marcus anything to add?
12:44 Priya Singh: No, that's it. Thanks.
12:47 Marcus Reed: No, good. Thanks.
12:50 Ari Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and invite.
12:54 [meeting ends]
